strain MFS2, which was isolated from a pork processing facility in the United States, was the most persistent strain in frankfurter product during refrigerated storage.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of PFEG to identify strains of L. monocytogenes is useful in monitoring persistence of strains during refrigerated storage.
strain MFS2 was the most prevalent and persistent Listeria strain among the five Listeria monocyto-genesis strains inoculated onto frankfurter products during the extended storage of the products.

strain MFS2, a serogroup I/2a strain, was the predominant strain of Listeria recovered from both frankfurters prepared from the formulation containing potassium lactate and frankfurters prepared using the control formulation without the added potassium lactate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PFGE is a powerful technique to identify the strains of Listeria present in food products.
pulsed-field gel eletrophoresis can be a very useful tool for monitoring the presence of specific strains of L. monocytogenes during the extended refrigeration of ready-to-eat products.
the use of PFEG is a useful tool for tracking the fate and survival of multiple Listeria monocycogenes strains in foods during storage.
